title: Sliding Vane Pump
model_title: Sliding Vane Pump (Eccentric Rotor, Cam Liner)

introduction.definition: A sliding vane pump has a slotted rotor mounted off-centre in a cylindrical liner; vanes slide in the slots and are pushed against the liner by centrifugal force, push rods or springs. As the rotor turns, the space between adjacent vanes grows at the suction side and shrinks at the discharge side, displacing a fixed volume per revolution. Vanes self-compensate for wear.
applications: Fuel and oil transfer, truck unloading

classification.configuration: Sliding vane, eccentric rotor, single chamber (unbalanced)

introduction.summary: A slotted rotor turns off-centre inside a cylindrical liner (cam). Flat vanes slide in and out of the rotor slots, pressed against the liner by centrifugal force (and often push rods or springs), so they form sealed chambers between rotor and liner. On the inlet side the chambers grow and fill; on the outlet side they shrink and push the liquid out. Vanes wear-compensate by sliding further out, keeping performance up on thin liquids such as LPG, fuels, solvents and refrigerants.

piping: Size the suction line for low velocity (viscous liquids need large suction pipes); provide a strainer.
Fit a pressure-relief valve (integral or in the discharge line) — a positive-displacement pump will build pressure until something breaks if the discharge is blocked.
Support piping independently of the pump.
For LPG: vapour-return line and bypass valve.
commissioning: Never start against a closed discharge valve.
Fill the pump with liquid (or ensure the suction is flooded) before start — avoid dry running unless the design allows it.

overhaul.task: Replace vanes and liner when worn.

video_tutorials.title: Sliding Vane Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Sliding Vane Pump.
A sliding vane pump has a slotted rotor mounted off-centre in a cylindrical liner; vanes slide in the slots and are pushed against the liner by centrifugal force, push rods or springs.
As the rotor turns, the space between adjacent vanes grows at the suction side and shrinks at the discharge side, displacing a fixed volume per revolution.
Vanes self-compensate for wear.
Typical applications include LPG, refrigerants and solvents (thin liquids); fuel and oil transfer, truck unloading; aviation fuel hydrant systems; hydraulic vane pumps.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Casing, Cam Liner (with Port Openings), Front Head, Slotted Rotor & Shaft.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Sliding Vane Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Sliding Vane Pump.
Check noise and seal.
Inspect vanes for wear (length).
Replace vanes and liner when worn.
Watch for vane wear / breakage: flow loss, noise. Common cause: abrasives, dry running.
Watch for vapour lock with lpg: no flow. Common cause: low npsha, warm product.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
